newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk secularist says government to be approved.
newsitem.headline: Turk secularist says government to be approved.

text.p: Turkey's prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz said on Thursday the president had vowed to approve a planned secularist coalition that would keep the Islamists out of power, despite its current lack of a majority.

"The president told me he would approve a government with the support of four parties," Yilmaz told a news conference in reference to four opposition parties, currently short of a majority in the 550-seat parliament.
Secularist Yilmaz has said he will present a government list at the start of next week to President Suleyman Demirel, who has to approve the bid before it goes to parliament for a confidence vote.
The defection of an anti-Islamist MP from Tansu Ciller's True Path Party on Thursday boosted Yilmaz's chances of success.
"Everyone must play a role in protecting the secular, democratic state at this time," deputy Isilay Saygin said in a written statement.
Saygin, who later joined the rival right-wing Motherland Party under Yilmaz, was the third MP to abandon Ciller since the president asked Yilmaz to form a government last Friday.
True Path is allied with the Islamists of outgoing prime minister Necmettin Erbakan who resigned last week under pressure from the secularist establishment.
Main opposition leader Yilmaz is relying on defections from Ciller's faction to win a vote of confidence in any government he sets up.
He needs to lure at least another six deputies from Ciller's alliance with Islamists into his camp and guarantee the support of 16 independents, most of whom favour him.
Saygin was one of two True Path MPs who refused to sign a document this week to pledge she would not vote for Yilmaz.

Yilmaz held a second round of talks with leftist leader Bulent Ecevit and other oppositon leaders on Thursday on forming the coalition. Ecevit, an avowed secularist, is tipped for a cabinet post in the planned government.
